utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. It has been a while since we were in court. We're here today. But let my first ask Madam Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before the Defence cases start, we have given an opportunity to the Prosecution to recall Mr. Rajcic. Is there anything that keeps us off from starting? Not. Then, Mr. Russo, are you ready to recall Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, thank you for coming back a long way to The Hague. We'll -- the Prosecution has asked to put further questions to you. Before we do so, I'd like you to make a solemn declaration, the same solemn declaration you made when you appeared for the first time before us. The text has been handed out. Could you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. Please be seated. You'll be further examined by Mr. Russo. Mr. Russo, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic. Nice to --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me begin by asking you if you are aware of what you will be testifying about here today?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: In principle, yes and no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Maybe you could clarify for me a little bit, "in principle." What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: On the 4th of March, a representative of the OTP phoned me and told me that I was supposed to reappear before the Tribunal. He told me that there were certain documents which I should have a look at again and provide an explanation thereof. On the same evening, on the Croatian TV, in a news report, I heard the same thing again, that the OTP had requested that I return here, in order to clear up or explain certain documents. That's why I said that, in principle, generally speaking, I know what this is about, although I don't know which documents are involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Mr. Rajcic, have you seen any HV artillery documents since the time that you testified here before?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. I haven't dealt with those matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could, please, Madam Registrar, have Exhibit D1447. And if I could have the assistance of the usher, I do have a hard copy for the witness, with the Court's permission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: This document tells me that it's a document containing a great deal of information, at a first glance, which formed part of the intelligence assessment of the -- of a battlefield. I'm reading the text on page 1 where it says "type of target"; then I can see that there are command posts of various levels, from, let's say, a company from numbers 44 to 50, an infantry trench -- or an infantry squad.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are target coordinates there as well, which is only customary. I can also see that the place of target contains a toponym or a place name. Another thing which I observe and which a customary form of such a list of targets as this one, as it says in the headline, is the -- the membership of a unit, whether it is part of the establishment of the Split Military District, and that's where the information came from, and was received by the intelligence department of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, have you ever seen this particular document before?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I saw this format when I was in Zadar, where the forward command post of the Split Military District was located, in the intelligence department there. This was a way of producing a, let's say, database of intelligence assessments of the theatre of war. One such list would serve to define targets that should be used by units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, are you interested in describing on how this fits into the whole system, or are you interested in hearing from the witness, as you asked him twice, whether he has seen this particular document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually interested in both pieces of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's proceed. It wasn't clear from your question to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I understand that from your answer, and correct me if I'm wrong, that you recognise the format of this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you say whether or not you have seen this exact document before?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: This particular one, I didn't. It says in the headline, list of targets of the Artillery Group of the 3 OG Zadar. In my view, it must have been created as a matter of urgency because they were short of time. In my view, it must have been made shortly before the start of the operation, because such a document should not carry the headline such as this one, list of targets, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you look to the bottom of each page, Mr. Rajcic, will you see the date as 30 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Zadar, the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you have any idea, Mr. Rajcic, who drafted this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: My assumption is that it was the intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you able to say whether this particular document was in fact used during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I can't state this with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what artillery group actually -- or the designation of the artillery group which actually operated in OG Zadar during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: If the document was used, judging by the place names or targets listed here, this was the area of Artillery Group 5, pursuant to the document enclosed to the main order for artillery for the -- for Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you could look at the items in the list and if you could tell us, if you know, which targets from this list, TS-5 actually fired at during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Last time, I said in respect of Artillery Group --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I have as a clarification on that are we talking about the -- at the strategic, operational or tactical level, because TS-5 was firing at different targets at different times for different purposes. So just for some clarification coming from counsel, would be helpful, I think, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was phrased in a rather general way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not making a distinction between the different -- if he knows what it fired at for whatever reason, I'm less interested in the reason than the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please answer the question, Mr. Rajcic. Perhaps you repeat it, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the target list, Mr. Rajcic, if you are able to tell us, if you know, which targets from this list Artillery Group 5 actually fired at during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I can't answer the question. I would have to have reports of Artillery Group 5 on the activity of the group. Last time I said I didn't have it. The only thing I said was that as part of artillery preparation, TG-5 fired at the barracks in Benkovac, and that -- and I said that was the extent of what I could say with certainty. As for other targets that may have been fired at by TG-5, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, in your testimony previously, you indicated that you had reviewed source lists of targets in order to plan and select the targets to actually be fired upon during Operation Storm? Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that when target lists were developed for operational and strategic levels, the basis for the development of such lists was a database from where the capital targets were chosen for Artillery Groups 1 through 5. I'm not saying this particular document. I'm saying a document, such as this one, containing a great deal of information would be used for the selection of targets for that level of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And looking at this document, can you tell us how it compares to the source lists which you actually reviewed? Can you tell us what the differences between these documents are, or what the similarities are, to the source lists which you actually reviewed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I mean, counsel has got a source list. I mean, if there's going to be some comparison with this document, I think it would behoove counsel to give the witness a source list that it received from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness can't answer the question because he hasn't got the information available, as he said before, then, of course, we will hear from him, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question, Mr. Rajcic. You've indicated that you reviewed source lists in order to select the targets for Operation Storm. What I'd like you to do is explain to us what the differences are between the source lists that you reviewed and this document you see before you. Any format differences or any other differences that you can note for us that would be of significance.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: When reviewing documents for the purposes of the government of the Republic of Croatia, I had at my disposal and developed target lists. For Artillery Group 4, 3, was something that we could find and this we couldn't find in respect of Artillery Group 5. We've established what the difference was between the targets chosen from a document such as this one and this particular document. One cannot discern any noticeable differences. What comes to mind when looking at this document, under 1 you have command post, or forward command post of the 92nd Motorised Brigade, Benkovac. Let's take it as a specimen or as a sample. When we select targets for the purposes of artillery and rocket groups from a database such as this one, this would be a capital high value target for Artillery Group 5 in Zadar. When I was working with my associates on this, using the same methodology we selected such high value targets for all artillery rocket groups. In other words, a type of target, a location of target, X, Y, Z and dimension of target if known.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move -- I'd like to look first, Mr. Rajcic, at some of the anomalies in this document. If can you look at the second page of the document, and this would be page 7 of the English translation in e-court. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I don't know whether I fully understood. You said you would like to look at some of the?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Anomalies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anomalies. Is that already if you'd just look at the content of the document instead of qualifying them already, would that not be the appropriate way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you can see, if you look, the target list here jumps from target number 87, on the second page, to 273. Can you explain why there are numbers missing from this target list, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Without having access to the entire database, and if this indeed relates to the area of Zadar, I don't know where the areas of Sibenik, Sinj and other areas of the front line are. I wouldn't really dare to venture giving an answer with any high certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So I take it, then, that you don't know what the 186 missing targets from this list are?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, unless I have other documents at my disposal as well. This document relates only to Zadar. I referred to a database covering the entire front line, from Mount Velebit, to Livno valley or, rather, Livno itself. It says "Operations Group Zadar." We had four operations group in all. I would have to go through them all, leaf through them all, and -- and then make a proper conclusion which would carry a degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you could please move to page 8 of your document, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 27 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You will note there, Mr. Rajcic, in the column for the source of information it indicates ZP for Military District and then it says "old one" in parentheses. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you explain what that means, which old Military District is being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I don't think that this relates to the old Military District. My view is that Military District in brackets "old" may refer to the fact that it was an old piece of information, because there was a constant flow of information in that area. I would conclude that this is an old piece of information which has been around for a while. That's what I would conclude by judging the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you offer an explanation, if you know, why, as of the 30th of July, 1995, this -- the information on these targets had not been updated?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I can tell you on the basis of what I know on the basis of my participation in the activities in the area, target 681 comes to mind. It says the other targets, Pijevcevo Brdo, target coordinates, firing position ZP Stari. In 1994, I took part in the development of a combat action which was supposed to take part in this area and there were firing positions there. You have type of target, P/ -- P, which stands for firing position. My guess is that this piece of information was left in the database as it was and it may have so happened that the firing position was captured by the enemy. That's why it remained as such in the database.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Moving back to page 2 in your original document, and that's page 7, I believe, in the English translation, will you notice that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think there's something maybe that needs to be clarified in light of the English translation of what the witness's actual answer was. This is page 10, lines --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's page 10, lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- 24 going into page 11, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll just read it to the witness. Mr. Rajcic, if you would be -- listen carefully and see what I now read to you is what you said. "My guess is that this piece of information was left in the database as it was and it may have happened that the firing position was captured by the enemy. That's why it remained as such in the database." That's the whole portion, Mr. Misetic? Is this what your answer was to the -- or at least that part of the answer was, or is there any inaccuracy in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not quite. Not my entire answer was interpreted. In other words, the firing position, Pijevcevo Brdo was captured for a while while I was a commander of the combat activities in that area. The firing position was -- or had been captured there and then later on that firing position was deserted. It had been left behind as a potential firing position that the enemy might capture again, and as such, with coordinates X and Y, it would remain within the database and it did remain in the database, and now let me just expand on that a bit. If need be, then we would already have preparations for the firing position and we wouldn't have to carry them out all over again. And that is why it had been left behind in this database as an old firing position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Referring back to page 2 of the document, Mr. Rajcic, and again this is page 7 in the English translation, you will notice that beginning from target number 273 going all the way to target number 661, no information appears for the Z coordinate of the target. Can you explain why there would be no information for the Z coordinate for any of those targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, I can only assume. One of the explanations could be that the source for this information considered that this was my biased opinion, my own opinion, and that it was not necessary to enter that in there, because in our security -- or, rather, intelligence department we had artillery information based on which we could easily determine the elevation of the target, if we had the X and Y coordinates. And it is my assumption that for this reason, the source that -- where it says source, the 34th Home Guard Regiment and the company of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, left behind this box unfilled, the Z coordinate unfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is the Z coordinate necessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, if counsel just correct one thing in the transcript. I think it came out the 34th Home Guard Regiment and I believe that it is the 134th Home Guard Regiment, if I'm not mistaken, that he was just talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Because, here, in the version that I have, that is missing, the -- the first couple of words -- the first couple of letters are missing. The copy is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you said 34th but you meant 134th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kehoe, when he said that, it would have been appropriate to explore whether he meant what he said instead of presenting it as mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Judge. I thought it was a translation issue, and my apologies and I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, is the Z coordinate necessary for accurate artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to us how exactly one would go about, as you indicated, discovering the Z coordinate information when it was not provided by the source?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, this is an method. What we did is, where we had a target, we would take the coordinates based on the topographical maps of various scales. If it was 1:50.000, a scale of that range, then it was less precise and one could determine the elevation of Z in metres. Whereas if the scale was 1:25.000 of this topographic map, then the precision would be higher, and once you marked the X and Y coordinates on the map based equidistances on the map we would work on determining the elevation of the target. If this would be between two isohypses -- or, rather, if there was a equidistance between them, we would interpolate the target. This would range from between 2 and a half to 5 metres, the precision rate, depending on the scale of the topographic map. If the map was 1:50.000, if that was the scale, the 50 metre difference would determine -- would be the difference. And wherefore if we had a scale of 1:25.000, then the precision would be up to 5 metres. So any person who was dealing with and working with topographic maps was trained and able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, looking at this document, Mr. Rajcic, can you tell us how it compares to an official HV document? Are there any markings that you would expect to find on an official document that missing from this or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: What official document of the Croatian army are you referring to? Do you mean an official document at a certain level, or do you mean an official document of artillery? From artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, an official HV target list, for example, would that bear any markings which are missing from this document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: No. An official document that we called a table of targets, of firing targets, the form would have been somewhat different. This table would be a bit different, would look different, and the content would also differ. The number that appears in the first column is the same, and then the type of target, X, Y and Z, and the dimensions of the target. The source would not be entered on a target list, nor would we enter this heading "can be observed" or unit goal, and I am here referring to a table of targets that was used by artillery units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in a table of targets which would actually be used during an operation, would the targets bear code numbers and not simply numbers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Both could be possible. The table of targets in itself would be coded for reasons of confidentiality, at least before the -- an operation begins. And then the numbers could be serial. They could be marked in this manner or in some other way. But in any case, it would depend on the level of the unit, whether this was the lowest level tactical unit, a platoon, battery, or division, and then, as you go up, you would -- you would enter some additional information, such as the azimuth, the base direction for firing, and such things. A list of targets of this type that we have before us, I assume that this was just an additional document that was used for the Artillery Group 5 [Realtime transcript read in error "35"] and not 3, as it says here, so that in the course of combat, at the request of the units to which the support was provided, one could act fast and have ready all the elements necessary for firing. I think I've went a bit beyond your question in my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine. I do appreciate the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions with respect to this particular document. However, I do have another document to put to the witness. I don't know if the Court wishes to address additional questions on this document before moving on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one question. I noticed that in the list the width and depth of the target is never specified, just an X. Was that common and what is the -- let me first ask you whether this is the ordinary way of describing the target dimensions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for us artillery men, it is normal to have -- it is -- to have a dimension of a target and this is not common practice, so I don't know why these Xs are entered here, and no dimensions of target were provided because it could have been pretty well defined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you further explain, what exactly means the column "Number of targets in unit"? What do you exactly understand by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the targets for a certain unit should be entered here in the area or swath of responsibility where that unit is engaged in combat operations to the left or right of the superior commander. Within this area, there would be various types of targets, at various depths, tactically and operationally. And here, there should be an indication of the number of units, for this let's call it X unit -- number of targets.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or in this particular case, for instance, the 111th HV Brigade, it should also indicate the number of targets for that unit at the tactical and operational level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit that it is not yet entirely clear to me. So you say it's the total number of targets within the -- that could be engaged by that unit? And then you're talking about your units, not enemy units. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I always mean the enemy targets. We don't have targets within our own units. These units are on the other side, at the enemy side. These targets --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- are on the other side, the enemy side, and we would obtain the depth and width of the target and for that unit there would be a target assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it is the number of targets that were identified in relation to the enemy units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And they are indicated as such within the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if I would take you, for example, to entry 491, and that is after a missing 30 numbers on the list, 491 and following. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There -- 491 and following, they're all, as far as the enemy unit is concerned is the 92nd Motorised Brigade and the numbers, although not with a huge range, they're all different. How do I have to understand? I'm afraid that I'm still not fully ... I mean, it is 147, 128, 149, 159, and if these are targets identified in the enemy unit, then what exactly explains the -- have you found it? I see that you're still ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, I am on page 4. And if I understood you correctly, I'm looking at number 491.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at the last column, it looks as if the enemy unit is the same in 491, 492, and that goes on until 499.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the numbers in the last column are not the same and I may therefore have not fully understood what this entry is and what explains the different numbers, although we are talking the same enemy unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we look at 491 and see that the command of the brigade is in Benkovac, that this is the Slobodan Macura barracks, and that that -- the source of information is the 7th Home Guards Regiment, and that this is within the area of responsibility of the 7th Home Guards Regiment, and that on the other side we have the 92nd Motorised Brigade. In my view, 147 indicates the number of the artillery target for the 7th Home Guards Regiment. Each unit had their own lists of targets, their tables of targets and their plan of fire, and they indicated those, the targets, with their own numbers and this was coordinated in coordination with their neighbour on the left and on the right flank, and this was done in order to avoid the overlapping of targets, which means that the same number could be used for two different targets; in this case there would be confusion. But in this way, we have the 7th Home Guards Regiment designating this as their own target designation, which is number 147, which does not necessarily mean that this is the -- this would be the same designation, the same target for the Artillery Group 5. So the same number does not mean that they have the same designation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So number, therefore, is the number within their lists. I now -- I think I better understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that would be on the target list of the 7th Home Guards Regiment of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I may have been confused and perhaps that could be -- an interpretation matter. Number of targets, I expect that to be a number, 10, 20, 50; whereas a number of a target on a list, then I would expect, as a matter of fact, that the singular rather than the plural. But I'm desperately looking at the parties to assist me in understanding what -- how you understood this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I mean, this can be checked but in the original it says number -- it's the singular, target, not targets --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- in the original. And in the interpretation -- in the translation it was translated in the plural. So it should be target number in the unit. Or number of target in the unit, not targets in the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if we find, therefore, I'm sorry, Mr. Rajcic, to -- For example, numbers 504, 505, then it apparently is the closeness, looking at the coordinates, which explains why they have the same number. Is that how I have to understand this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Or the communications post is within the building that's -- in other words, 505 could be located within 504.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, without any width or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The coordinates are not exactly the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and if we do not know the width or the ... Okay. I'm just trying to understand what is ... Mr. Rajcic, first of all, thank you for clarifying the issues and the parties have further assisted me. I was a bit misled perhaps by the plural which --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is one issue, just for the interpretation, and it's page 16, line 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 16, line 10. Then I have to go back to the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just find it. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the number in line 10. I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not there yet. One second, please. 16, 10. Yes, I've got it in front of me. Yes, could we ... you said at a certain moment -- and please complete what is may be missing or which is not incorrect. I read part of your answer. And it was a question about code numbers. At a certain moment you said: "A list of targets of this type that we have before us, I assume that this was just an additional document that was used for the Artillery Group 35 and not 3 as it says here. So that in the course of combat, at the request of the units to which the support was provided, one could act fast and have ready all the elements necessary for firing." Is there anything not accurate in a portion of the answer I just read to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood this properly, it is not Artillery Group 35. That is something that seems illogical here. And if I said that, I apologise. I said that the Artillery Group 3, the Operations Group Zadar, should have in fact been Artillery Group 5, because this was an auxiliary means for fast action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That clarifies the issue. And is also in line with my recollection. Whether translation or transcribing issue, it has been corrected now. Let me just see whether I have any ... No, if I have any further questions I will keep them for a later stage. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could just ask that we have revised translation uploaded to indicate the correct designation for the final column which Your Honour questioned about. I assume that is not going to be a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it avoids further -- Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could please have 65 ter 7160. And if I could have the assistance of the court usher, I also do have a hard copy of that document for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this document while I was selecting documents for the purposes of the government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber what this document is.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: This is a war diary or a war log-book of the commander of a -- an artillery group. It sets out the dynamics of actions as they played out in his particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us which artillery group this relates to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Artillery Group 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you could look at page 2 of the document, and that's the same in the English version in e-court, at the entry for 1100 hours, and it lists you as the individual reporting. And it indicates the turning of two 130-millimetre guns. Do you recall reporting or ordering the turning of those guns for TS-4? Sorry, Mr. Rajcic, we need a verbal answer.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you could move along to page 6 in the document. That's also the same page in the English version. Page 6 at the entry for 0915 hours. And this is an entry which is 0915 hours on 5 August. And it again lists you as the person reporting and simply states Ocestovo, times 5 pieces. Can you recall your involvement with that particular entry?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I apologise, page 6 in my batch of documents, doesn't contain the entry. I have a different type of numeration. One page was skipped. I have 2, 3 -- or, rather, followed by 4, 5, 6. Page 3 is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies there's actually -- it's page 6 in the e-court version. It actually says page 5 at the bottom of the one that I'm looking for for you. Because it appears that the actual third page has not been numbered, so there has been a number skipped in the actual numbering in the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: At 9.15, Marko Rajcic, Ocestovo, 5 pieces. Is that what we're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Can you explain that entry for us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: This means that on that date, there was fighting. I was in direct contact with Artillery Group 4 and in the area of Ocestovo, there was fighting going on, and the unit engaged in infantry combat was supposed to receive support from a 130 gun because 203 Howitzers from Artillery Group 4 did not have this particular location in their range.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what exactly the target was in Ocestovo that you ordered the firing on?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: This was the road from Kistanje to Stara Straza. Perhaps a kilometre and a half ahead of an intersection from Stara --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter didn't catch the name of the location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to Padjene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the semi-last location you referred to. The interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ocestovo is a larger area across which the Kistanje-Stara Straza road runs. The location which was fired at along the road was, according to what I can remember now, a kilometre and a half away from an intersection of roads from -- of the road from Stara Straza to Padjene.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber why you fired on that particular location, the one kilometre from the intersection?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Based on the information from the field, the enemy was pulling out, together with their military hardware. The assessment was that in the area of Padjene, they would be setting up their second defence line. The goal of the fire was to make it impossible for the enemy to possibly set up another defence line in the area of Padjene in an organised fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to page 8. That's the same in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is, the number 7 will appear on the bottom of that page in your handwritten version, Mr. Rajcic. And at the entry for 0930 hours on 9 August, it lists you as reporting the firing of 36 130-millimetre shells at the general area of Srb. And I would like you to explain to the Trial Chamber what exactly it was you were firing at at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: In the general area of Srb, at an intersection of roads between Licki Petrovac or -- I will have to think about the location. This was an intersection of roads in Srb; to the east was Licka Kaldrma, and to the left, there was a road leading to the springs of the river Una. That was Donji Lapac, yes. It was Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us why exactly you were firing 36 shells at that particular area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: For the same reason as before. It is only customary when the enemy's pulling out with military hardware in combat that one should make sure that the enemy is prevented from organising a defence and putting up resistance, which may lead to further casualties and materiel damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you have information at the time that the enemy was in fact attempting to set up a defence line, or is this more of a preventative measure?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Information was received from the 4th Guards Brigade to the effect that elements of the artillery -- or, rather, members of the artillery units of the 4th Guards Brigade clashed with the enemy in the area, and they used infantry fire. In other words, there were groups of enemy forces which, although routed, were still dangerous for our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You'll see the very next entry on that page, which is for the date of 12 August, indicates your ordering the firing of 25 shells of 130-millimetre cannon at Drvar. And I would like you to please explain to the Court why you ordered that firing.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: The intelligence assessments we had at the time indicated that, from the direction of Drvar, a counterattack would be launched against our forces in the area of Bosansko Grahovo. That was the intelligence we received, and the intelligence came from various sources and was obtained in various means, indicating that the enemy forces in Drvar were regrouping and building up with possibly engaging in a counterattack. The counterattack did in fact take place, and in the area of Bosansko Grahovo, we had 24 soldiers killed. This particular action had the following goal: Between Bosansko Grahovo and Drvar into the depth of the enemy, artillery fire was supposed to use -- to be used in order to stop the enemy from advancing, and in order to allow us to organise ourselves properly and engage in proper defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, can you tell us what exactly in Drvar was fired at by TS-4 on your command?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: The road intersection. The lay of the ground on which Drvar sits is such that it allows only for two good quality manoeuvre exits for the forces; that's Bosansko Grahovo and Bosanski Petrovac. It was these particular roads, exit roads, that we controlled with our fire, in order to prevent, disturb and harass the enemy in their attempt to pass along the same road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you could move to the third page that you have there, the one which actually doesn't have a number at the bottom. It's the third page in e-court as well. There's an entry for 1520 hours which states: "Vlahov, T-130 for OG Sinj." Can you tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Since I'm quite familiar with the entire area where we engaged in combat, this means that the communication went through the then chief of artillery for Operational Group North. The Operations Group Sinj was supposed to receive support on the orders of the commander of the Sinj Operations Group. Unless I'm mistaken, this was within the area of responsibility of the 6th Home Guard Regiment, Biocici. This was supposed to be done according to the coordinates that were entered. In other words, the newly arisen target -- or, rather, in other words, this had to do with a target that had arisen as combat went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And because it was a newly arisen target, is that why we find the actual coordinates written into the diary at that point?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. If there is no numerical designation, and if is not contained in the target list, this was the proper form in which newly arisen targets would be entered into a document of this sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And staying on that same page, looking at the entry for 1545 hours, it states that: "One shell in the middle of T-130 gun carriages. No one injured." Do you recall Artillery Group 4 taking a shell hit during the operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. And not just here. This was for the second time, I believe, that it involved Artillery Group 4. We had another similar situation on the first day that the enemy engaged Artillery Group 4. I'm familiar with this particular event, because I would receive timely information on events such as this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. You have indicated that you've both reviewed this document in the past for your work for the Government of Croatia and also that you were in real time overseeing the operations of Artillery Group 4. Is there anything that you found in this document that does not correspond to your recollection of events during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: If we are discussing matters that do not tally with the report of Artillery Group 4, I can tell you that while I was reviewing documents at my disposal, I observed a difference between the number of times Artillery Group 4 opened fire and the requests addressed to Artillery Group 4 from the Sibenik Operations Group. The numbers didn't tally there. In my report, the document that I produced, by way of a confirmation of the work I did, I made a note of the fact that there were discrepancies as to how many times and at what intervals Artillery Group 4 opened fire, as compared to the number of requests it received to open artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could please show the witness Exhibit P2341.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at the screen, is this the document, the report to which you were referring where you noted the discrepancies between the requests and the reports of Artillery Group 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. This was not notified that we were going to go into this document. We had numerous conversations and e-mails over the past week, and, as a matter of fact, I was informed in no uncertain terms by Mr. Russo very adamantly on Friday that he was going use two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not actually going to use the document. I didn't realise that the witness was going refer to this. I'm just trying to confirm that this is the report to which he is referring that he has already provided the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said something about reporting. If, Mr. Russo, if that's the purpose question, just to identify when he talked about reporting whether he was referring to this report without going to the content of it, then it would clarify and would not put you in a difficult position, because we would just better understand what his answer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. It may be very well given that that I have go back into this but I have to take a look at it at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Russo, so your question to the witness was ... Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at the document on the screen, is this the report to which you were just referring a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a part of the report on page 1, and that's what I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would move for the admission of 65 ter 7160. That's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections from the other Defence counsel. Madam Registrar, that would be number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit P2533.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think the best thing to do is to have a break now and then continue after the break. Could I receive estimates from the parties, now knowing what the examination-in-chief has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will probably be about two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And as it refers to Markac Defence -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Higgins was on her feet. If you would not object, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies for not being polite and especially towards a lady. I wouldn't expect more than 30 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that there's a fair chance that we would finish this morning. We'll have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I take it that the Defence has seen the decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the Chamber last Friday --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which may have an impact on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what we expect to you do, or what you are -- what you will question the witness about. Mr. Rajcic, you will now be cross-examined or further examined by Mr. Kehoe, who is -- well, you know Mr. Kehoe is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before I proceed. With regard to P2533, I did not object before. There are a few word changes in that document. That's the Milin diary. I can sit down with counsel and resolve it. There are a couple of words missing but there's nothing of any major consequence, but I just want to mention that before I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll hear the outcome of your conversations with Mr. Russo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic. Mr. Rajcic, we were talking --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were talking this morning with Mr. Russo about the list of targets that you had where it notes at the top TS-3, that's D1447. And TS-3 was -- at the time of Operation Storm was TS-5. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony this morning, you mentioned a database and in fact in your -- I'm just corrected. Just so I clarify that it was renamed TS-5 at the time. So it was TS-3 and then it was renamed TS-5; that's right? Yes, you have to say --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony this morning and in your prior testimony, and this is at page 16.329 at line 2, you talked about the production of a database for various targets. Do you recall that sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And one of the individuals who assisted greatly in the production of that database was a Mr. Marijan First; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Marijan First, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Pardon my pronunciation, Marijan First.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Marijan First was -- what was he in the scheme of things?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was my assistant. In operational terms, he was the assistant for artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us a look a little bit and explore this database and this is -- this was a database that had been compiled with information over a significant period of time, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- if I can show you a hard copy and -- as well as hand some out to the Chamber and counsel. If I can direct your attention to 1D00-1062.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And for the purposes of clarification, Mr. President, there was a document that was given to the Office of the Prosecutor by the Republic of Croatia and has since been turned over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, if you could take a look at this particular document. And it's in an A-3 form. Do you recognise this format, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This is the format that was used whenever this was computer processed. A-3 and A-4 were the usual formats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is -- as opposed to the document that we looked at this morning that Mr. Russo gave you, which was listed by ordinals numbers, 1 through -- certainly there were some gaps in it, but 1 through, I believe, 87. This is a listed by coordinate values, isn't it? And coordinate values being the Y, X, Z coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. I should actually take a look and see whether it was in the normal order as things as the targets were distributed. If we have, for instance -- if we look at the first one, the 6th and 7th coordinates, we can see that both X and Y are increasing or incrementally or they should be decreasing. That's the normal order of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is to compare these various targets to prevent duplication and see if the various reporting agencies were talking about the same target, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in any case, each target has its precise coordinates, and that's the only coordinates they can be. They can't be different. The only thing is we can designate three different numbers for three different users. But the coordinates are always the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, as we look at this, I mean, we have sources of information over in the second-to-last column, and those entities are the entities that are reporting to you the particular targets in that area. For instance, on page 1, it's the 134th.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, the Home Guard Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll get into a little bit more of a comparison with this as it related to the list we talked to this morning. But I'd like to talk about some general topics first. And if you could just look at this document and just page through it with your eye on the operative group at the top of the page, and I do believe that the first ten pages of this document reflects that these are targets with their coordinate values for Operative Group Zadar. Do you see that? Look at the top of the page for the first ten pages. It may actually be 11 pages. Ten? Ten. They're all for OG Zadar, right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, Operations Group Zadar. And as for the target, judging by it, I recognise this area, and I claim that it is -- it was in the area of the Zadar Operations Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we continue on to -- from pages 11 to 12 we have a listing of targets for Operative Group Sinj.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And then, lastly, from pages 13 to 18, we have a series of targets for Operative Group Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now I just note by way of clarification, in this entire document if we look at the lower right-hand corner, this document is prior to the document that you reviewed this morning, D1447, as it is dated 12 April 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this document indicates that these three operative groups had these targets within their geographical area, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this morning, you were asked a question by Mr. Russo, and if I can just point to the area, and we noted in -- we don't have to flip back for it. utterances.text: Now let us turn back to the large A-3 document that we discussed previously and let us go to, if we can, the first page of OG Sinj, and that would be on the right upper right-hand corner, 06397160, and you see in that page alone there are any number of numbers between 87 and 273. utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me backtrack just a bit and maybe I just went a bit too quick -- too quickly. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be page 11 in the B/C/S. And page 28 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but for Operative Group Sinj, I see pages 1 and 2, not 11 and 12. And for Operative Group Zadar, I have 10.

utterances.text: Okay, but just stay with that -- just stay with that page. The first group on Sinj. Okay. Now in that first page of Operative Group Sinj, you see many numbers in the right hand -- in the left-hand column between 87 and 273, do you not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, I have to intervene again. That's not what it says here. I see a series of 470, but these numbers are not in sequence.

utterances.text: Exactly. Now, they're not in sequence but if you go down the list of those numbers, for instance, if we go to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, the ninth one down, it has number 126. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now 126 is, of course, we don't -- there's not a question on this, of course it's between 87 and 273. utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I think there's a missing foundation. This -- perhaps the witness should remove his ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not certain that it has been established or yet put to the witness that the numbers which are on this document are in fact the numbers which are missing from the document which we looked at previously. The witness testified during direct examination that he didn't know what those targets were. And so to now put this to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to be very practical in this respect. What you apparently want to establish, Mr. Kehoe, is that the missing numbers are not in the same operative group and we find them somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the sum and substance of it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try to do that. First of all, what one could do is to look at the numbers. I tried to find, for example, some of the numbers on this list and they were all missing on the other one but this is, of course, only a -- I'm talking about Sinj. This is, of course, I haven't had any opportunity to do it systematically. May I take it that you have done that systematically?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any numbers which appear both in the Sinj list and in the Zadar list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can tell you I didn't find any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't find any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I will go back and look more thoroughly, but I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it would give us information on two levels. First, if we do not find any, that there's a fair chance that the lists perhaps not for the full 100 percent but are complimentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's one. Second, if we would find one, then, of course, we could look at the description of the target which would give us some information as to whether we are talking about the same thing. It could still be coincidence that the numbers do not match, but if we would find -- well, let's say, 487 saying firing position and if in the other we would find 487 being a bunker with different coordinates, then -- so, therefore, to a large extent, this information can be obtained from these documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not by me and not in three minutes. But by the parties. Mr. Russo, I take it that you -- while that your concerns that we're trying to establish what these two lists can tell us, even if it has not been established, Mr. Kehoe, also let's ask whether the witness knows anything about it. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge. Just one clarify -- if the witness knowing anything about ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if he would know about this numbers and then you could point 15 and then say 119, I see it or I don't see it. Is there any overlap; if there's not an overlap, that at least makes it -- increases the likelihood of the lists being supplement -- supplemental to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we do find them to see what then the list tells. So you if you would please focus on what the witness knows and -- well, it might --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, if I can -- I was just informed by one of my colleagues who did do the list there is no overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's not, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The second issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good. And that's -- Mr. Russo, you can -- you may have all the time to verify that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That the -- the second issue is I didn't want to limit this to just OG Sinj. If we look back at OG Sibenik, those targets also fill in some of the gaps that are in the OG -- the OG Zadar list that we had this morning, D1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also no overlap?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's comparing lists -- if the witness knows anything about it, of course, please ask him. If he doesn't know that much about it, let's focus on our analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Russo, may I take it that this more or less addresses your concerns as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO

utterances.text: Now, just going back and looking at this. You're familiar this type -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they do.

utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1459.

utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to continue ask you some questions about the document that we were reviewing with Mr. Russo, D1442, and I would like to just discuss with you some of your testimony and some of the maps that you did on Benkovac. utterances.text: And if we can go to 1D00-1138. Mr. President, what we have here and I -- just by way of explanation is, and we will just start with the first document that comes up on the screen. And as we move sequentially through this, we have done it for Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac. If we can do the first one first, please.

utterances.text: Now, as you can see, the green markings -- or the -- the circles are the circles that you made, Mr. Rajcic, and the green markings are the grid coordinates -- and the blue markings, I take it, the grid coordinates from the list, D1447? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: And the marks that you had, that you put on this document when you were being examined by Mr. Russo were markings you took from your recollection as targets that you recall were fired upon in Benkovac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. The general area where the barracks, the police station, and the intersection were. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did that based on recollection without actually looking at the specific grid coordinates that you now have before you that were taken from this D1442; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me just clarify one thing with these targets and we'll go into this a little bit differently. utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: It is correct to say that they were planned to be fired upon, not the ones that were fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. And that's you plan ahead of time so you don't have to do the geometry during the course of combat; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a methodology of preparations to be made for combat, depending on the season, depending on whether the hardware was supposed to be repaired, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in addition to targets that you had at the Military District level, if we look at the list that Mr. Russo was talking about this morning, there are numerous targets that are listed there that are tactical targets, aren't there, that battalions and brigades would fire upon at a tactical level; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. If the markings in blue indicate the contents of the list, then this was intended for the operations level.

utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he said about the tactical level.

utterances.text: Could you please repeat what you said about the tactical level so that the interpreters can catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The targets marked in blue, if my understanding of what Mr. Kehoe said is correct, were taken from this list that I have before me, and they were targets located in the general area of Benkovac. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rajcic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I just need to make a clarification. It is uncertain to me if the witness -- he keeps saying "if my understanding of what Mr. Kehoe says -- if this is correct." I'm not sure if the witness is saying this is what is actually the case or his understanding if that's what's being put to him. I'm not clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the answer is clear but I will do -- endeavour to talk about firing at a tactical level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now the decision to fire at a tactical level is being made by lower level commanders, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just turn to the next slide. And for clarification purposes, again we are dealing with Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we did this for clarity purposes so Your Honours will see the area from Google Earth where these targets are on the grid coordinates, so ... If we can move to the slide which is -- again, we have done the same thing and we're talking now about the Obrovac area. And the circles that you have -- and, again, you discussed this during the course of your testimony. And you noted the items that are -- and that's -- in the Obrovac area he was talking about, on 19 February 2009, again, at 16.326, line 3, through 16.333, line 10. Again, you listed the bridge and a cross-roads in 673 and the cross-roads at the bottom which is designated as 693. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the markings in green.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, 674, 673 and 674.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now there were in fact the other targets in this list. If we look at the top, I believe it is 670, the Glinice factory, 355, an artillery firing position we have on the screen. We look at the left-hand side of this document, 338, combat accommodations. Those were entities that were not fired upon at the Split Military District level. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I'm not able to say whether fire was opened because I don't have that information in regard to Tactical Group 5, although I know that as part of preparations it was not planned to open fire. The later artillery support fire was directed or ordered by the competent unit as combat progresses. That's why I'm unable to say whether fire was opened or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's look at number 670 on your list which is the Glinice factory.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Which page is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That would be -- if you go just through these numbers, it's 670, it would be list page 8 at the lower left-hand corner. Do you see that, 670 which is the -- in the --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Glinice factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look that factory, that it notes that it is a Military District old list. Old source. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, based on that information there, was it your recollection that that the Glinice factory was not fired upon even though it was on this list of targets?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I don't think it was fired upon, the factory, because it was visible from the surrounding hills. There were not many units defending the position. I think it was only a squad that was there. But this particular location was listed among the targets where the forces were expected to have the strength of up to a platoon. It was merely entered into the database as a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk about these entries into the database just a little bit, and let's talk about them in terms of Obrovac. Now, Obrovac was near the front line, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And near the front line position that was manned by the ARSK, there were any number of tactical positions or tactical targets for the HV forces that were going to move towards the ARSK, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's just demonstrate that with the next slide, because, again, what we've done on this slide with the Obrovac near the front line --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can we go to the next slide please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We have basically given the confrontation line. And as you can see from Obrovac, in the middle of the page, there are any number of targets that are on the list that we talked about this morning with Mr. Russo. Now, those are targets that are going to be fired upon, if necessary, at a tactical level, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn to the Gracac map, and that would be -- your testimony on that score was again on February 19th, 2009, at 16.361, line 13, through 16.366, line 8. And this is, again, we have taken your document, which is P2329, and overlay it on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, could we go back to the previous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- map for a second so that I have an opportunity to digest it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies there, Your Honour. The blue line is the HV line. The red line is the ARSK line with the zone of separation between. I didn't elaborate on that sufficiently. But I left it -- it's in the legend on the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: About the confrontation line, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. If we can go to the next -- back to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, what we've done here as I noted just for the record this is it P2329, the map that you had, that you -- and we overlayed it on targets for Gracac. And I believe that you designated from that several targets in a factory and a cross-roads. Now, your recollection on this, I believe, was not entirely clear because your batteries weren't firing on this, is that right? utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, with regard to this, I mean, Jagoda does list -- there were in fact any number of targets as we see here, or potential targets as we see here, in the list that we talked about this morning. But you don't know if they were fired upon or not. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just turn to the next page. Again, what we did was overlay -- or take out the actual map and just give an idea of these targets in contrast to Gracac itself. utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't object. utterances.text: Mr. President, if we can just go back to map I can clear it up in a second. If we can go back to map 4, if we can. And let's look at, for instance, what we talked about before, if we can go to the list and look at 346.

utterances.text: If you could you turn to 346. That's a good example as any, I would think. utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you with me on the list itself of targets, 346, which is -- which is page 4 in the B/C/S and page 12 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you see, even going down from the top of the page, 337 all the way down, we have a series of targets, 346 being a fortified trench, 347, fortified trench, et cetera, and that information, if we go to the source of the information, is coming from the 84th Guards Battalion, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and that is a tactical target for the 84th Guards Battalion, and not for the Military District; isn't that right?

utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's in the disposition of the 84th Guards Battalion, or right ahead of the disposition or the deployment of the forces of the 84th Guards Battalion.

utterances.text: So what we're talking about is, if the 84th Guards Battalion is moving on an offensive, if they deem it necessary, they want to hit this trench prior to moving forward, don't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, with their assets.
