utterances.text: Once again, Your Honour, we'll offer this document, this map into evidence. I don't know if we need any further clarification but I will be guided by any advice counsel can give me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My only issue is that the legend indicates, for example, green Military District targets. I don't know if that is intended to indicate targets which the source of information is the Military District, or if, in fact, the witness can answer whether these were in fact targets for the Military District level. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And can I answer that question with regard to Obrovac. The witness answered what he recalls was fired upon. These particular targets are taken from the document that we were talking about this morning, D1447, and when we look at the source of information, it will be the Military District. That's the designation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, what we find on this map, the numbers and the descriptions, is that taken from this Jagoda list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, verbatim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything -- verbatim. May I then take you to the same map. 672 is close to the centre a little bit up to the right, 672 enemy unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I look -- but it could be a translation issue, but if I look at the Jagoda list, 672, it says other targets Varos, Simici, without any description on whether it's an enemy unit or -- who has added this information to what I find on 672? Or is it the -- I'm looking at the one Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I see what Your Honour is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the list that was used this mourn, the Jagoda list by Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see that -- on the map I see information which does not appear in that list. 672, enemy unit, and I have not checked yet the coordinates whether that is really Varos, Simici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I just check with my colleague? Just one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is our mistake. I have to go back and check this one again more thoroughly, but that is our mistake. My apologies. We have attempted to try to take this with the numbered designation as accurately as possible, but that is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you will understand that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- descriptions as other targets without any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- description are perhaps more intriguing than firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or ... Now how to proceed. Because then -- of course, this could be just one mistake. It could also be that it's not -- what we find on these maps is not in every respect reliable. The reason why I checked it, Mr. Kehoe, is that on this Jagoda list we find sometimes other targets or a lack of a description; whereas, on the maps I didn't find any one, which raises another question, is whether all the entries of the Jagoda list, in the area covered by the map, are depicted or whether there is a possibility, that, for example, there are other targets or there are -- is it complete. Is there -- could you find on this list any coordinate and a number attached to it, which does not appear on the maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can tell you that -- that we have attempted to make a good faith effort on this particular area. We will go back and re-check it thoroughly, given this mistake and whether or not there are any other targets on that list. We did put some effort involved in putting this together, and I can tell you, Your Honour, Mr. President, that we will check and by Wednesday when we reconvene, if we can just MFI it now, we will ensure that everything in here is correct and if there, in fact, we missed a target that is in this geographical area that is not depicted and I will share it with co-counsel prior to coming in here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Russo, you would agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the MFI number for this series would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1460, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn our attention to another topic that addressed this morning with P2533, which is the diary for TS-4. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: You're referring to this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am, sir. Yes, that's the one. Yes. I referred to it by P2533, so the woman that is typing over there in the corner and everybody knows what we are talking about. I'm interested in exploring with you some of the entries that were discussed with you with Mr. Russo and specifically the ones that were discussed on the 9th of August, 1995. The first being at 9.30, where you requested 36 pieces of T-130 to be fired in the general Srb area -- or it says Srb general area. I should -- I think it is probably the last page in the B/C/S, if I'm not mistaken. Maybe the second-to-last page. It is. The second to last page in the B/C/S. Do you see that, sir? Now, just by --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now just clarifying this, I mean, as we look at Srb, I mean, Srb is in Croatia, and just --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just to the east of Srb is Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when we look at the 9th of August, 1995, there was in the general Srb area, in this theatre of war around Srb, there was combat still going on, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Still going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the combat was taking place, for the most part, in Bosnia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: For the most part, Operation Storm was on the territory of Croatia but the final stages were also on the territory of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm talking about as of -- let's talk about --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Talking about the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th. The theatre of war included Bosnia-Herzegovina, right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. And in smaller parts, Croatia, on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just go down the next entry and we are talking about you calling in 25 pieces of T-130s on the 12th of August to Drvar. Do you see that? Mr. Russo talked to you about that this morning?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Drvar was the headquarters for the 2nd Krajina Corps of the Bosnian Serb army, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So at this juncture in time, and we are talking about between 9 August and 12 August, you now have a Serb force which comprises, in part, the Bosnian Serb army conducting an offensive against the HV; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, they were -- they, in fact, conducted the offensive in which the HV lost, I think you said, 24 men on the 12th of August; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in an attempt to fight back is this shelling that you talked about in the -- on the 9th as well as the 12th, an attempt to repel Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: To repel them and stop a possible -- prevent a possible counterattack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in fact, Mr. Rajcic, shortly after the 12th, the counteroffensive by the Serbs was stopped, and the HV began their attack again, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. It was stopped in the area of Bosansko Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And throughout all this, of course, the person that was commanding this at the highest level was General Gotovina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think I'm through, Mr. President. If I could just check with my colleagues. I did finish in much quicker time than I anticipated but ... If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions of Mr. Rajcic at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, the Defence of Mr. Cermak has no questions for you, from what I understand. Therefore, Mr. Mikulicic, are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in order to avoid being repetitive, I will have no questions for Mr. Rajcic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No questions. Mr. Russo, has the cross-examination, because that's what it mainly came down to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- has that triggered any need for further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could again bring up D1460, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, looking at this map here, you see different targets plotted. The ones in blue, do you know whether or not those targets were actually fired on during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I only know about the Slobodan Macura barracks, because the -- the firing was planned for the Artillery Group 5, so I know of that. As for the others, I don't know anything about it. So there was an artillery preparation for an attack on Slobodan Macura barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the other -- the targets in blue, if those in fact were fired upon or planned to be fired on during Operation Storm, would you have received any reports or notifications that anyone had fired on those positions, whether they are at the tactical level, operational level, or any other level?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I would only have received it if there were some major disturbances in coordinating the combat, as far as artillery is concerned. As for the firing of targets -- on targets at the tactical level, through regular channels, each tactical unit was supposed to prepare a written report, and by way of their operative centre, they should inform the forward command post in Zadar thereof and in Sajkovici. That was the pattern. Then an analysis of the targets engaged would be done, who engaged the targets, and in such situations we -- I would know whether there was fire opened on a target or not. I've already said that on the 4th of August, and the 5th in the afternoon, I only received information that the Artillery Group 5 had fired during artillery preparation on the barracks Slobodan Macura.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And rather than taking you through each one of these slides, does the same situation apply with respect to the areas of Obrovac and Benkovac -- and Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. For Obrovac, when I marked the plotted targets the last time, this was in the period of planning for the combat. Now, in the course of the combat, the artillery group or the remaining part of the artillery group, which had remained after a part of it had been set aside for the needs of the military police, the 130-millimetre guns could not reach Benkovac [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think I would like to take you back to the answer you just gave. Where you read -- let me read it back to you. It reads that: "In the course of the combat, the artillery group or the remaining part of the artillery group, which had remained after a part of it had been set aside for the needs of the military police, the 130-millimetre guns could not reach Benkovac?" Is that correct? Is it military police?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Not Benkovac; Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can I just clarify one point that was just raised there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, just staying on this map that's on the screen, which is D1460, MFI, for Benkovac, and we have, for instance, at the bottom that 696 is a road, 953 is a cross-roads west, 743 just straight above that is an artillery firing position. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You -- if those positions were fired upon during the course of the day at a tactical level, absent a large disturbance, you wouldn't receive reports back or you wouldn't have been notified at the time that they were in fact firing on those positions, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. That question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was just -- what was -- the issue that was brought up on redirect examination was an attempt to somewhat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If these targets that you mentioned that are marked in blue were engaged at tactical level, I described the manner of reporting. The information would be collected at the operations centre of the forward command post in Zadar, where they would be analysed, and if there were some disturbances then such information would be forwarded to the main command, General Gotovina in Sajkovici, or me and the officers in the artillery administration. If not so, then there was no need to send any reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back to the -- to the entries in the diary which you were asked about before. That is, the 36 pieces fired at the 9th of August to, as you described, the Srb -- no, as described in the diary Srb general area. And then the 12th of August, the Drvar, 25 pieces. Could you give us some more details about when you gave these orders, or at least there were perceived as your orders or written down as your orders, to -- to fire 36 pieces of the -- to the Srb general area. Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: At the time, I was at the forward command post in Sajkovici. I apologise, excuse me. In Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The firing of 36 pieces is reported as at 9.30 in the morning. Could you give us more details about when you received information, what kind of information it exactly was, and in which way you phrased your orders?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: On the night between the 8th and 9th, we received information that there were still some remnants of the army of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina in the area of the cross-roads, around the cross-roads, and it was necessary to advance with our forces, because the president of the Republic of Croatia had ordered that we should reach the state border. Which means that the Croatian army, on the 9th of August, had not fully completed that order because the border was nearby, and we -- to get there, we had to go through Srb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I stop you there for a second. You said there were remnants of the forces there - let me just find your exact wording - "some remnants of the army of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina." Could you tell us more? Was that 100 people? Was that -- how organised were they? What type of information did you receive?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the numbers or the formations as organise -- as the structure units. What information we did have was that there were troops amassing in that area. Our forces had to advance and reach the border and, of course, what followed was the normal procedure, which also included artillery support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you have any information as to the weaponry used by those troops?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: There was information that there were pulling out their artillery, parts of their artillery. Parts were left behind and we found them on the road. And, of course, the assumption was that the artillery that they had with them will be deployed somewhere in that area and used against us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said artillery were left behind. Was there any artillery fire, one party to another, reported to you at this morning? Well, let's say, from the last 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've already said that in the area of Srpski Klanac, which is south of Srb, an observation post, an artillery observation post of the 4th Artillery Brigade had been attacked.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 4th Guards Brigade, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you describe the attack, what happened, what kind of weapons were used?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I cannot describe it because I was not at the artillery post. Other than the information that I received from the operations centre, I didn't have any other information. The information was that this observation post had been attacked by artillery, either by tanks or artillery pieces, that were still part of the army of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina, and this was the reason why they had to be neutralised, those assets. In other words, that that part, those remnants of the -- that the army that had been, as it was, those remnants, and -- received another psychological blow and lost, as it were, the will and desire to fight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was anything reported as where the artillery fire came from, or tank fire? You said artillery or tank fire. Which direction? From -- within Croatia; was it from Bosnian territory? Could you tell us what was reported to you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: After an analysis of the terrain and the topographic maps, you can see that Srb is between -- is nested between high peaks and there is not much room to develop forces on the left and right flanks. The only possibility that remained was that this should be done on -- along the road which they were taking to pull out. And based on the information that we received from the first combat lines, or deployments of our lines, we understood that this was around the cross-roads, the -- in the general area of Srb, leading to Lapac or -- from the north towards Bosnia, Licka Kaldrma and Drvar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any -- apparently in this clash, you describe it as tank or artillery. Were the positions finally identified from where the -- your unit was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is standard procedure, or, rather, they didn't have enough time -- the enemy forces did not have enough time to conduct this properly, to have engineering fortifications built and so on. In such situations, these things are just hastily organised, in order to prevent the enemy from advancing quickly through the area of attack that had been designated. In other words, this would be done along a road, in a garden, in a backyard, or whatever, and in this way, they would fire back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you ordered that -- was, in these clashes, were there any casualties on the ARSK side?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: According to the information that I had, I don't know that any dead soldiers of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina were found there. I don't have that information, or, for that matter, of any civilians. And, of course, now I'm just referring to the area that we are now discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how wide would that area -- I mean, if soldiers on the other side would have been killed you would have found them, or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not my role, nor was it my task, nor was I supposed to do that at the level where I was. So I was not meant to receive such information, such feedback. I would not be the first instance to receive it, if there had been some dead enemy there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any casualties in these clashes among your people?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were one or two slightly wounded soldiers, wounded by fragments of some shells or maybe some infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those wounded were members of what unit or what ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I think they were members of the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you describe what then happened. These pieces were fired, the 36, apparently. Did you receive any report on the effect of what was hit, what the results were in ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, I can only say that the results were such that the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina left that area, and a few officers and I flew over that area in a few helicopters. We landed in Srb. We couldn't see anything. Our job was to reconnoitre the area and decide how to re-deploy the tank pieces. And there was only one minor incident. Fire was opened on our helicopter from small-arms fire, and there were -- there was no -- there were no consequences of that fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 36 projectiles fired, did they hit the target, as you described it, before? Since you flew over the area, could you give us some more details about what the effect of this firing exactly had been.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: In the area that was targeted, as I passed by the intersection in a hurry, I saw several explosion-caused craters which led me to conclude that the unit opened fire upon the targets that were intended. Of course, I did not investigate in respect of each and every projectile. It was impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on in the days that followed. What happened between the 9th and the 12th exactly, which caused you to -- to give the order on the 12th? And I would like you to talk about it in chronological order. What caused you to -- to give an order to fire on Drvar, 25 pieces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I will try to reconstruct the events of the 9th through 12th on the basis of what I remember. On the 9th, on the order from General Gotovina, I was supposed to use the 112th Brigade, 7th Home Guard Brigade and 134th Home Guard Regiment troops in order to take positions along the state border in the area of Srb. I went back to the headquarters of Artillery Groups 4 and 5, the ones that had redeployed to the area of Srb. They had 130-millimetre guns and I ordered them to take up fire positions in the village of Kupirovo, south of Srb, in that general area. Then, on the orders from General Gotovina, I went to the forward command post in Sajkovici, and I was given the task of technically dismantling the forward command post, since a group, the Operations Group East, Istok, was set up in Bosansko Grahovo. Operations Group West was in the making in Srb. As I was engaged in dismantling the forward command post in the village of Sajkovici, I received from intelligence officers of the Split Military District in Knin the particular piece of information that I referred to before, to the effect that the enemy had been regrouping their forces in the area of Drvar, in cooperation with the Bosnian Serb Krajina, the 2nd Krajina Corps, and that there -- and that it was quite likely that they would be launching a counterattack against us in the area of Bosansko Grahovo. For that reason, artillery pieces were fired at 8.30. 130-millimetre guns were used. These were guns of the Artillery Group 3 which were still located at the firing position in the village of Luka, next to Bosansko Grahovo. As I've already said, the goal of the fire was to make sure that in the pass south of Drvar, in a canyon there, we should prevent the enemy forces from advancing, since they had been there regrouping and reorganising themselves. On that same day, in the afternoon hours, I travelled the area from Bosansko Grahovo to Knin. Towards the evening hours, I met General Gotovina at the headquarters, and he told me and gave me an order. He said that a counter-attack had been launched in the area of Bosansko Grahovo, that there were quite a few casualties involved. He told me to take the battalion which was left in Knin of the 7th Guards Brigade, they were left there as an intervention force, and to head back to Bosansko Grahovo. We should have carried out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes. You said for that reason artillery pieces were fired at 8.30. That was on the basis of intelligence. Earlier you said something about that you had lost 24 of your men. When was that exactly?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it happened on the 12th, in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you lost your 24 men before you ordered the 25 pieces to be fired at Drvar. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- what I said is not -- yes. In the afternoon of the same day, where in the morning, you gave orders to fire at Drvar. I take you back to the 9th. Engaging a cross-roads, would that, under normal circumstances, take 36 pieces?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Under normal circumstances, it would depend on the strength of the forces on the other side. If we take the standard norms of the eastern option, artillery fire would be used in order to neutralise the enemy, to disturb or harass the enemy which, in that case, would involve 10 percent of ammunition expenditure for neutralising 25 percent of the infantry forces at the target of the artillery pieces. The target being in an open area and not fortified. Now, one should calculate how many projectiles would be needed to neutralise such a target, or, rather, to neutralise 25 percent of such a target, in order to be able to say that the 25 projectiles were in fact only 10 percent of the entire amount. So that would involve a bit of maths. I don't know if we have time enough to go into these calculations now or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then again me what exactly the target was for the 36 pieces.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Based on the information from the intelligence organ, the enemy forces could have been 100, 200, or 300 who were regrouping and building up their forces. These, together with the VRS forces, that's to say, the 2nd Krajina Corps, were organising their forces with a view to launching a counterattack. This type of target can be qualified as a target of the strength of an artillery battalion, and the dimension of the target would be 300 by 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When Mr. Russo asked you questions about what triggered your order on the 9th, you were talking just about infantry fire. Some remnants. You didn't say a word about artillery; you didn't say a word about tanks. I read it to you: "Information was received from the 4th Guards Brigade to the effect that elements of the artillery, or, rather, members of the artillery units of the 4th Guards Brigade clashed with the enemy in the area and they used infantry fire. In other words, there were groups of enemy forces which, although routed, were still dangerous for our soldiers." This is a story which is certainly quite different from the answers to the questions I put to you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, among other things, I said, for example, that there were elements, and I don't know this if this was correctly interpreted or not, of soldiers who were members of artillery units as well as infantry soldiers. In other words, there was a presence of the military in the area. The observation post was also attacked by infantry fire as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask the parties whether, in the earlier answers given to Mr. Russo, whether artillery or tank being used in these clashes were part of the answers. Could there be any translation issue? I thought I would have heard of you if such an important ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is possible. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can check that. Mr. Rajcic, we have fortunately the ability to check in quite some detail your own words and how they were translated and how they were transcribed. At least the way in which it was translated to the Chamber, it was just infantry fire of some remnants, which were mentioned as the event triggering your first order on the 9th. I think in your -- when I asked you about it, you were talking about intelligence as well; whereas, in your earlier answer, you just referred to information received from members of the 4th Guards Brigade. Was there any other intelligence as ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is very difficult to describe combat action in two sentences, a day's worth of combat actions in two sentences. The fact of the matter is that between the 8th and the 9th, fighting was still going on, though, admittedly, not of high intensity. Doubtless there was fighting going on and this is the sort of information that reached the command post. If I were to describe all the activities taking place in that general area covering some 10 square kilometres, that would be very difficult. I'm only citing details, warranting artillery fire on the 9th. Still, if I made myself clear, what I said here was that there were reasons to open fire and that there was still sporadic fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to focus specifically on the -- on the order given on the morning of the 9th. I just put to you: Would it have been possible that members of the artillery units of the 4th Guards Brigade had a clash in the sense of some of infantry fire fired at them from an unknown number of persons shooting? Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is one type of action in the field of artillery which is called adjustment and guidance of artillery fire in movement. In other words, the commander of the artillery unit is at the forward end of the disposition, among the infantry troops, and guiding fire from there. To me, that comes across as a customary combat action. Whether it was indeed carried out or not, I don't know. The information that reached me at the command post was that there were such problems and attempts were made at solving the problem. And that's quite legitimate. The 4th Guards Brigade, ever since it broke through on Mount Dinara, had that sort of fire guidance in movement, as it advanced. Those are the forward ... May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said sort of fire guidance. What do you exactly mean? Guidance given by whom? Or by what?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Guiding of fire is something that is done by forward spotters or forward observers. Oftentimes fire is guided by the commanders of the units opening fire. In this specific case involving the 4th Guards Brigade, it was the commander of the artillery battalion of the 4th Guards Brigade who engaged in guiding artillery fire south of Srb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we read in the document that you gave the order. The 36 pieces. And that's what I'm focussing on. That you gave the order. So, therefore, to explain what a local commander would do or would have done is beyond the focus of my question.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, my apologies. A local commander, or a lower level commander, as we call it, is the one who seeks support -- fire support from his superior command, along his axis of attack. For this reason, the information reached Knin. When we relocated the command post from Sajkovici to Knin, we received information there to the effect that they needed artillery support in that area. That's where I come into play. My role comes to the fore. I call the commander of the artillery group, which contains 130-millimetre guns, and we give them the assignment of providing support to the unit which found itself in difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Do you remember in which way you -- what the -- what wording your order was? Because it appears on paper now as general area of Srb. Was that what you told them to do?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: If I were to state now that I remember this 100 percent, it would not be fair, I don't think. The way I worked always was that one would take the relevant coordinates from the map of the location and the coordinates would be placed into the target -- through the target analysis calculation because that is the only way we can do it. Otherwise, fire cannot be opened, unless we get the X, Y, and Z coordinates first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, on paper, where in the diary usually the targets are well identified, either by code or by coordinates, here we find a description which is far away from such a precise description of a target. Do you have any explanation on why they would have written it down in the way they did?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a working document produced by the commander of the artillery group. He would write down the initial information, the source information, out of which everything that is relevant for artillery fire is extracted. I wasn't there when this was done. It is said the general area of Srb. The X, Y coordinates indicate the intersection. What follows next is one would take the coordinates down and open fire according to the coordinates. The way it is written now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: -- it does not allow for artillery fire to be opened. There has to be the rest of the information, including the X and Y coordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. Just see whether I have ... I have one or two more questions but we'll have them after the break, because we, first, need some time. We'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I have a few more questions for you. Could you have a look at the list that was presented to you by Mr. Russo this morning, the one we called the Jagoda list. Do you have it? And then I'd like to take you to entries 735 and 736, if you could try to find them. Have you found them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at these descriptions, which is "other targets," and then just the name of a village, and that's true for both 735 and 736, and nothing else is found there as what type of target that would have been. Is this kind of describing targets familiar to you, and how do I have to understand them, other than in the village or the village, as such, there is something to be targeted? I'm just wondering how this can be used and what purpose it serves.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honours, for these targets, one would need additional information and explanation. I can say exactly what it was because I know what was in Popovici, and we see the coordinates here, and this is enough for an artillery person. But as for tactical and technical preparation of the goal, one would have to know whether this is a place where troops have accommodation or maybe a depot, so one would need additional information, and this information would be sought from intelligence services, which would then have to provided confirmation as to what type of target this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you would need additional information, and you say: "I can say exactly what it was that" -- it seems not to be transcribed in -- "because I know what was in Popovici." Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. In Popovici there was a reserve contingent of the army in the area of Karina. These were forces that conducted a defence in the area of the Operations Group Zadar. I spent a lot of time there, and I'm familiar with Popovici because they were frequently mentioned, and that is why I can say here now that this was reserve contingent of the army. And I have also added by way of explanation that if you didn't have this information, if you didn't know it firsthand, then additional information would be required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said: "I spent a lot of time there." When do you mean, you spent a lot of time there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, I arrived there in early June 1993, and remained in the area, the Zadar-Sibenik area through the end of 1994, or, rather, to be more specific, until the 5th of November, 1994, when I moved on to Dinara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my understanding, Popovici being a target in the area territory held by the Serbs, when was that taken by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: It was taken by them, as far as I know, from the very start in 1991. They were already there in Popovici around the Karinski [phoen] sea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I asked -- you said, "I spent a lot of time there," and when I asked you when, you said it was in early June 1993. You were then staying in Serb-held territory?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: In 1993. No, I know this area because I served as a soldier in the Benkovac barracks and I also conducted military exercises there, while I was in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to understand. You say, I know about it because there was a -- you spent a lot of time there, and you said there was a reserve force there. When did you learn about that reserve contingent of the army?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I learned that information in June 1993 that there was a reserve unit of the army of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was in barracks, in -- how are they -- and where were they exactly located in Popovici?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Well, the standard practice was for them to be billeted in some school buildings or some other type of warehouse or company facilities or in private homes, if facilities of this type were not -- non-existent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we see that on this list often described, school which are always understood which as school where there was military presence, not school children; that's how I understood it. Or warehouse or -- usually you find that in a description laid out, what kind of facility it was. Even I think that the issue of what a stacionar is, there couldn't be so many hospitals, I'm afraid, Mr. Russo, but, please, correct me when I'm wrong, that seems to be a place where people are -- where military men are housed or located and we have seen that many of them were close to the confrontation lines. But here I found nothing. Where your explanation is an explanation which usually comes with a corresponding description on the list; whereas here it is -- it doesn't say anything. Do you have any explanation for all the other targets without any description? Sometimes from the location, for example, if it says an elevation, then I take it that it's a higher point of military importance. But, here, village. What explains the absence of any further details, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot explain it because this is not a document that I produced. This is a document produced by the intelligence organ. But, as I said, an artillery person would need to get some additional information and that is what was usually done. That's how we actually did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. Mr. Rajcic, have you ever been invited by the Prosecution to be interviewed prior to coming to The Hague and testifying?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you mean today or earlier on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier, in the last, well, anything in the last ten years. Did they say, Mr. Rajcic, would you please come and talk with us, we'd like to interview you. Did that ever happen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, it happened on four occasions. The first time it was in 2007, when I received a phone call at home. It was from a woman who said she was a representative of the OTP of this Tribunal, this honourable institution, and she asked me if we could talk and I said that I didn't feel it was -- I thought it was not serious enough to -- that it was too serious to conduct this type of conversation over the phone and that I was prepared to do it but not over the phone. On the second occasion - that was on the 21st of November, 2007 - on this occasion, two investigators came to my parents' home - that's where I live now - they came unannounced and asked that I appear on the 22nd in Sibenik for an interview. They asked my mother to sign off on the summons for my presence at this interview. She refused. And since I was not at home, when I arrived in the evening, I found this summons in the house on the table, and it was a summons for this interview. And I arrived -- and I arrived at the county court in Sibenik at around 9.30, I believe, this was. I think I still have this document in my archives. And my intention was to tell these gentlemen (a), that it was really inappropriate that they should come to my parents' home in this manner; and (b), that I was not prepared to answer any questions because I had placed myself at the disposal of the Defence of Mr. Gotovina, and I volunteered that I would gladly testify on their behalf, if they found it was necessary. And if this Honourable Tribunal wished me to report and to come and testify in some other manner, that I was prepared to, of course, respond to that. Then there was another -- there was another telephone call this year on the 22nd of January -- the 27th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: To the effect that the Prosecutor would like me to testify on 16th of February and whether I was prepared do so. Again, I replied that I had already stated how I was prepared to testify, at whose request, and if this Tribunal sent a subpoena, or subpoenaed me, that then I would of course appear in court. This is what happened last time and it went the way it went. And then on the 4th of March this year, I received another phone call from the Prosecutor at home. They asked, they said that I should come and testify again, because some new documents had been obtained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that is the telephone you referred to earlier when asked about -- recalled whether you knew about which documents. Or is that a different -- earlier, I think Mr. Russo asked you whether you would -- was right at the beginning of the -- is that that telephone call [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, yes. Yes, that's the telephone call I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You have explained that telephone call and it was not an invitation for an interview but rather to be recalled as a witness. Could you tell us, when did you agree with the Defence to make yourself available as a witness? When was that; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: As early as 2005, I think in January, I gave a first statement to the Defence, and I also certified it, and the -- my statement had to do with my recollections of the Brioni transcript, and I think that this Chamber has that at its disposal. And on this occasion, I also offered to testify, if needed and when needed, on behalf of the Defence in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for those answers. I have no further questions for you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, you were asked some questions by Judge Orie concerning the Bruno Milin report, P2533, concerning the shelling in the Srb area. I want to direct your attention just briefly to one of the annexes that you had previously talked about, and that is P2343.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could bring that up and I would like the English page, which I believe is 45. I'm not certain exactly what the -- the -- 52 would be the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is the Srb -- excuse me, this is the 4th Guards -- it's the operative log-book for the 4th Guards Brigade. I'm not certain if you recall it in your annex, but I believe it was Annex 13. Now, on the -- let me just pull this up on the B/C/S. I'm looking for the entry for the 8th of August at 8.05, and there's a request in there that the TRS - that would be the one of the artillery groups - is requested to work over Srb. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that's a request to fire on Srb, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's stay on this -- on this date and go down to the entry for 1430, later on in the day. I think we're going to change the page in the B/C/S, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could change the page in the B/C/S to 1430. Frankly, I don't know how many -- there it is, at the top, the second-last entry. The second-to-the-top entry on the B/C/S; it's the second from the bottom on the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now this reflects at 1430 that: "Mechanics, oil and fuel wanted for captured vehicles -- captured tanks," excuse me, "and infantry combat vehicles at the point A11 (Srb)." Now, did it -- were you given information or did you get information at the time on the 8th, prior to your order on the 9th, on the 8th, that there was fighting going on with the ARSK and that tanks were captured -- and infantry combat vehicles were captured from the ARSK during the course of that combat?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: The precise information as to the type and quantities of captured vehicles and technical equipment did not reach me. We just -- general information that there were captured -- there was technical -- captured technical equipment and vehicles, but I could not speak about the details but that there were some vehicles and technical equipment captured. I knew of that general information, and it was immediately used in combat around Bosansko Grahovo and so on. So, for me, this is something that is routinely done during combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were also getting information that combat was actually taking place between the HV and the ARSK on the 8th, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Such information always was done in coordination and they were relayed as quickly as possible, depending on the communications equipment that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's keep going on this date and turn to the next page for the entry of 1940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which page in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think it would be the next -- 26? 46. 46, I think, in the English. Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 1940. Nurses' reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you remind of the exhibit number, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This exhibit number is P2343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2343. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes that the members of the 3rd Infantry Battalion - of course it's part of the 4th Guards Brigade because this is the 4th Guards Brigade operative log-book - wounded in the area of Srb. That should be S-r-b as you can see in the actual on the translation, although it's difficult to see. But in Srb are Nedjo Paic and Ivan Matic. They were also lightly injured by a hand-grenade. After he's given first aid, Paic returned to his unit, whereas Matic stayed in the hospital -- stayed in hospital. Ivan Marunica was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can we turn the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Also hospitalised today. He will check out tomorrow. Gavran and Lucaj have been evacuated to Split." Now, was this consistent -- while you might not have the specifics, was that consistent that the HV had suffered casualties in the Srb area on the 8th, at the hands of the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. And it says here in the evening hours and that's what I have already mentioned here, that there was combat, there was fighting going on. There were casualties, and we were supposed to reach the state borders and, of course, on the next day, we were preparing for artillery preparation and so on. So I don't want now to specify all the things that are done in situations like these.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it was the following morning, according to the Bruno Milin document, P2533, the TS-4 diary, that you ordered fire in the Srb area at 9.30 in the morning with 36 rounds. That's what we talked about before.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was -- now, I think you established before that was an attempt to fire on these ARSK positions, wasn't it, and drive them back and or harass them and drive them away, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milin, you think you noted that you didn't write this. Mr. Milin doesn't have specific coordinates and Judge Orie asked you questions about those coordinates. I mean, were you firing pieces of artillery, T-130s, in this particular circumstances without grid coordinates and without a specific target? Were you doing that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, throughout the duration of the homeland war, I never fired a single projectile without knowing the exact coordinates, nor did the units I was in command of, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So simply because Mr. Milin didn't write the grid coordinates down one cannot conclude that there were no grid coordinates, could you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: No, nor could it have been possible to have the necessary elements for targeting, if there are no coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to the next entry in the diary which is 8.30, from Drvar, and you, on the -- 8.30 on the 12th of August of 1995, where 25 rounds are being fired on Drvar. Now before we get to that I would like to you look at the bottom of the rest of the page, where there are numerous notations concerning events that have taken place from the 10th through the 12th. Do you see those at the bottom of the page? Or it should be actually the --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the entries that we have here are not necessarily in chronological order per the handiwork of Mr. Milin, are they? Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let us turn our attention back to Drvar. I mean, I think you mentioned both in my questioning and in questioning by Judge Orie that Drvar was the headquarters of the 2nd Krajina Corps. And that you fired on Drvar on 12/8/1995 at 8.30. Let us turn our attention to what the response of the VRS happened to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can go to P71, which is the Split Military District diary, and the date [sic] I have is 101 in the English and 62 in the B/C/S. That's P71.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I'm looking at the time entry at 5.45 on the top of the page on the 13th. Do you see that, sir, at 5.45?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now at 5.45 on the 13th, the enemy - and this is the VRS and the ARSK - started to attack HV forces in the area of Grahovo, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in addition to infantry, this notation reflects that there was an artillery attack as well, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you were preparing or when you were making a decision with your other commanders to fire on -- on Drvar on the 12th of August of 1995, were you aware that VRS was attacking and that they continued to attack into the morning hours of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. In this part of the front line, the army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina launched infantry and artillery attacks all the way through to Glamoc while building up forces, the ones that I referred to earlier, in Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The reality, Mr. Rajcic, is from the -- your entry on the 9th until at least the 13th of August, 1995, there was heavy fighting in this border area between the HV and the combined Serb forces, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Russo, well, perhaps before, Mr. Rajcic, on the last question you answered that it was heavy fighting, whereas earlier you used the word "sporadic" for that area. I'm a bit confused about your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not too long, please. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I talked of sporadic fighting, I referred to the area west of Grahovo. Let's take Grahovo as the centre of the area. To the east there was sporadic fighting and the HV conducted attacks against Glamoc. Admittedly, the positions of the sides did not shift, save for the Grahovo incident where I said that we lost 24 of our men. If you can visualise Drvar and Grahovo, to the west of Grahovo we have sporadic fighting all the way to the state border where there was Operation Storm; and to the right flank we had our forces, together with the HVO, where there was continued fighting, and let me call it stationary fighting, and exchanges of artillery and infantry fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have P2343 brought up again and go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, perhaps I should have -- it's your witness so perhaps I should have given you the first opportunity to, but usually the Chamber's questions come after the re-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have page 53 in the B/C/S and page 45 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the entry for 0 -- for 8th of August, the entry that Mr. Kehoe directed your attention to, which indicates the tanks had been captured. This happens at 1430 hours on the 8th of August, correct, and the firing that you reported or the firing that you ordered on Srb doesn't occur until 9.30 in the morning the following day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Doesn't say "on Srb." It says "Srb general area," counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what it says and that's what I understood Mr. Russo wanted to refer to. But for your information, it was the order about the 36 pieces to be fired at the general Srb area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you explain this to us then. If tanks are captured in the area at 1430 hours on 8th of August, what happens between then and 9.30 in the morning the following day? Because if you look on the very next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It's entries for 9.30 -- the entries for 9 August only begin at noon on the 9th of August. So this document doesn't provide us any information about what happens around the time that you ordered the firing. So if you can tell us what happened between 1430 hours on the 8th of August, when the tanks were captured in the area of Srb, and when you ordered the firing.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: If we go back to the earlier document, it says Knin 1440, captured tanks, and a supply of fuel for them was requested. The fighting continued in the direction of Srb. At that point, on that night when the soldiers were wounded at 1940, in view of the continued fighting, the need arose for artillery preparations to be made on the following morning, and to complete the assignment as ordered. Not all the tanks and artillery pieces were left behind by the enemy forces, and not in one location. They withdrew with whatever vehicles, tanks or whatever they had, and depending on the fuel they had. Some of the artillery pieces were therefore transported into Bosnia. Not all were left behind in Croatia, based on the information I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Were there tanks or artillery pieces of the RSK remaining in Srb, after those which were abandoned and taken by the HV forces at 1430 hours on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: I myself saw a T-34 tank in the vicinity of Otric, as well as several army trucks full of ammunition. In Srpski Klanac there was a 76-millimetre gun complete with ammunition but without the towing vehicle. Probably the intention was to speed up the pace of retreat and to make room for soldiers to be mounted on trucks. This is what I saw personally. As for the quantities that were there, you can look into the files of the Split Military District, into the files listing the military hardware captured during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, those pieces which you are indicating you personally witnessed, the T-34 tank, the army truck, ammunition, those were abandoned pieces of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Re-called]
utterances.text: Yes. In the area just ahead of Srb, not in Srb proper. As I was on my way to Srb, this was between Knin, Otric -- if you can visualize it it is easier for me because I know every inch of the ground. All of it that was found was in the area up until the Srb pass, or Srb canyon. That's south of Srb proper along a stretch of some 10 to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, since it appears that no one has any further questions for you, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming back to The Hague. It's already the second time that you were here, and for answering the questions that have been put to you by the parties. You are excused. I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There were a few outstanding matters. We do not really have time to deal with them. At the same time, I would like to see to what extent we could -- we could finalise them. Perhaps without coming back to court and spending a whole session on it. There was an issue of D1083, deals with a translation issue on a document, rules of internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior. There's still -- I don't know whether that has been resolved. Mr. Mikulicic, wasn't it you who --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that issue was in fact triggered by the Defence and it was on 65 ter list of the Prosecution, and I spent a lot of conversation with Mr. Waespi in order that they simply ask for the clarification of the remarks that the defendant made on it. And, unfortunately, in this moment, I have no further information on the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's any progress made, perhaps the Chamber could informally be updated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will check with Mr. Waespi on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there was -- yes, there was another matter, but the Chamber will -- there was still an outstanding issue on the relevance on the judgement issued by the municipal court of Knin in a complaint matter which was instituted by -- I think by (redacted) and others. It has been tendered, I think, through Mr. Hedaraly. The Chamber will decide on the matter. I think the main objection was relevance. It was about war damage. Yes, the Chamber was informed that for Mr. Lazarevic there are no requests for protective measures and that still was there to be put on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the qualifier, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That there was a specific issue about his residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So no protective measures apart from that everyone refrains from referring in any way to the place where he resides. That's on the record. There is another matter which is primarily P2336, P2339, and P2340, are -- and let me turn into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We adjourn until Wednesday, the 27th of May, 9.00 in the morning, when the Pre-Defence Conference will be held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
